_source: sequential eval run 6 (docs/evals/2026-08-04-run-6.md), 5/5 cases, 19/19 checks; parallel runs excluded — API contention inflates per-case durations 2-6x (run 3 finding)
_policy: soft ceilings: run-evals.sh prints 'within'/'REGRESSED', never fails the case; update ceilings after each accepted sequential run
_metrics: Three ceilings, because each catches a regression the others miss. max_seconds is wall clock. max_usd is the CLI's own total_cost_usd — the real cost, and the only one that catches a model-mix regression (a sonnet -> opus re-tier keeps token counts flat and triples the bill). max_tokens is attributed.total.tokens — a work-volume proxy that is invariant to pricing, which max_usd is not: Sonnet 5's introductory rate expires 2026-08-31, so a max_usd breach can mean a price change rather than a regression. The rate-table reconciliation in <case>.cost.json is what distinguishes the two.
_tokens_caveat: Run 6 measured token totals as >99% cache-read tokens in all five cases (e.g. n-plus-one: 3,666,860 cache of 3,669,451 total). Cache reads bill at 0.1x input, so max_tokens tracks context volume x turns far more than it tracks spend. Read it as a work-volume signal and let max_usd speak for cost.
_bimodal_cases: `policy` and `action` each run two ways: the coordinator fast path takes the case (fewer stages, much cheaper) or it delegates. Run 5 delegated `policy` (994s) and fast-pathed `action` (420s); run 6 did the exact opposite (`policy` 381s undelegated, `action` 1217s across 4 agents). Ceilings are seeded from run 6 with headroom, NOT inflated to cover both modes — so on a REGRESSED reading for either case, check <case>.cost.json's agent list for delegation before treating it as a regression.
_opt_in: `feature` is registered but excluded from the default sweep (OPT_IN_CASES in run-evals.sh): it is the only case guaranteed to delegate, and also the most expensive, so it opts in when coordinator behaviour changes rather than costing every sweep. Its ceilings stay null until its first accepted run.

n-plus-one.basis: run 6: 302s + headroom. Creeping hard across runs (96 -> 157 -> 178 -> 302) and it breached the previous 250s ceiling — the ceiling is raised to keep carrying information, but the creep itself is run-6 finding 1 and is the thing to explain, not to absorb
n-plus-one.usd_basis: run 6: $1.82 billed + ~30%; no delegation, single opus-5 lane

policy.basis: unchanged from run 5's 994s. Run 6 took 381s because the case did NOT delegate — leaving the ceiling at 1100 keeps it valid for the delegating mode rather than making every delegating run read REGRESSED (see _bimodal_cases)
policy.tokens_basis: run 6: 4,371,934 undelegated + ~30%. A delegating run will likely exceed this — check the agent list first

action.basis: run 6: 1217s across 4 agents (qa-engineer, main, tech-lead, backend-developer) + headroom. The previous 600s came from run 5's 420s fast-path run, and its basis note predicted exactly this: 'if the fast path stops taking it, this reads REGRESSED the first time it delegates again — that is the intended signal'. The signal fired as designed; the ceiling now covers the delegating mode
action.tokens_basis: run 6: 9,699,200 across 4 agents + ~30% — the most expensive case in the suite
action.usd_basis: run 6: $5.16 billed + ~30%. 41% of the whole run's $12.50

tests.basis: run 6: 633s, within the existing ceiling — unchanged
tests.tokens_basis: run 6: 3,697,406 + ~30%, of which qa-engineer was 1,978,501 across 39 tool calls

hygiene.basis: run 6: 106s (scrum-master, read-only ledger scan), within the existing ceiling — unchanged
hygiene.tokens_basis: run 6: 579,315 + ~30% — the cheapest case, and the only one on haiku

feature.basis: unseeded — opt-in case, never yet run. `action` is the closest comparable at 1217s in run 6
feature.tokens_basis: unseeded — expect the largest in the suite; it delegates across 3-4 specialists
feature.usd_basis: unseeded — `action` billed $5.16 in run 6 for a comparable shape
